responses.tool-purpose: Adapts source text into accessible reading materials and related study prompts.
responses.problem-solved: It helps staff create easier entry points into dense academic readings.
responses.feature-interest: Using one article to produce a simplified handout and discussion prompts.
responses.test-request: We asked Diffit to turn an assessment-design article into a simpler student-friendly version.
responses.test-what-happened: The simplified text was helpful and the prompt suggestions were usable after editing.
responses.surprised: The accessibility features felt more valuable than the prompt generation.
responses.corrected: We removed a repetitive question and edited one explanation that slightly distorted the source meaning.

strengths.text: Makes difficult texts easier to approach.
Produces support materials quickly for preparation.

weaknesses.text: Generated prompts can be repetitive and shallow.

opportunities.text: Could support inclusive access before seminars.

threats.text: Complex ideas may lose nuance if teachers skip review.

responses.learning-improve: It could help learners meet a threshold understanding before deeper seminar discussion.
responses.teacher-time: Adapting source text and drafting quick support questions.
responses.avoid-use: Avoid it when precise wording and disciplinary nuance must remain unchanged.
responses.check-before-use: Check whether simplifications preserve meaning and whether questions promote genuine understanding.

quadrant-map.rationale: It saves time and improves access, but still requires review to manage the risk of oversimplification.

responses.ai-decisions: It decided which concepts to compress and which vocabulary to scaffold for the reader.
responses.human-judgement-needed: Educators must decide whether the adapted reading still aligns with the learning outcome.
responses.concerned: A novice teacher might mistake accessibility for accuracy and overlook missing nuance.
responses.other-educators-know: The educational value depends on active teacher editing rather than one-click output.
responses.view-change: We ended more positive about its accessibility benefits than its question-writing ability.
